title: Bringing Legal, Security, IT and Finance in only to approve or block the finished product
summary: Design a workable route for responsible experimentation with the people who own its constraints.
diagnosis: Late review turns foreseeable requirements into apparent scope creep and encourages a false choice between speed and control. Early participation is useful when it identifies the real boundary: which data, actions, costs and commitments the experiment may involve. It is not useful when every exploratory question becomes an open-ended approval queue.
diagnostic_questions: Which functions will need to accept the operating result, and what information do they need now?
Is there an approved low-risk experimentation path with clear data and spending boundaries?
Which unresolved requirements could force a redesign after users have already adopted the prototype?
proposed_actions: Hold an early use-case review with a concrete workflow and action/data map rather than a generic AI presentation.
Publish supported tools, allowed data categories, spending boundaries, escalation routes and review criteria for common experiment types.
Invite risk and support owners to help design acceptance and incident tests; resolve disagreements through a named business decision-maker.
working_artifact: Experiment operating agreement: permitted tools; input data; allowed actions; budget; users; review gates; evidence needed for scale; exception route; responsible owners; stop procedure.
measures: Lead time to an informed review decision and frequency of repeated requests caused by unclear requirements.
Late redesign caused by previously undiscovered data, procurement or operational constraints.
Participation in the approved path, including anonymous or non-punitive reporting of why teams bypass it.
tradeoff: Early involvement does not guarantee every proposed experiment should proceed. A legitimate safety or confidentiality concern is not merely resistance to innovation. The aim is an explicit, timely decision with feasible alternatives where possible.
illustrative_case: Illustrative application: a team may test extraction on synthetic invoices immediately, while access to live supplier banking details requires a narrower service identity and a separate review. The experiment can progress without ignoring the boundary.
